items.title: Prepare Your Business for Siri AI with Apple Business Connect

items.content_html:
With the arrival of Siri AI, consumers are increasingly relying on intelligent assistants to automate daily tasks and quickly discover new information. To ensure your business gets noticed by these AI agents, it is essential to be indexed where they look first.

The most effective way to do this is through Apple Business Connect—a free resource that allows you to manage your company’s presence across the Apple ecosystem, including Maps, Wallet, Mail, and Siri AI. By utilizing this tool, you can customize your local listing with actionable features like reservation or ticketing buttons, ensuring customers see the most accurate and important information.

How to Get Started

  1. Visit the Website: Go to the Apple Business Connect website and click the blue “Get Started” button.
  2. Enter Business Details: Enter your organization’s legal name, business email, website, and address.
  3. Create an Account: Create a Managed Apple Account by providing your name, email, password, and phone number.
  4. Verify Account: Verify your account using the codes sent to your email and phone.
  5. Set Preferences: Agree to the terms and select the options that best fit your business size and goals.
  6. Manage Profiles: From the homepage, you can begin managing your Maps profile, Wallet profile, and employee IT tools.

Verification and Next Steps

Before diving in, verify your organization by clicking the banner at the top of the page. You will need to provide two verification documents, such as a business license or domain verification.

Once verified (typically within five business days), you will unlock a full suite of free branding services, including:

  • Location management
  • Branded Mail
  • Tap to Pay on iPhone
  • Brand Profiles

Apple Business Connect is a powerful, free tool to help you get discovered and connect with customers faster. Don’t get left behind as new AI technology rolls out—get started today!

items.title: How Beeper Can Help You Detox from Social Media
items.summary: In a world where social media algorithms are designed to keep us endlessly scrolling, finding a way to disconnect without losing touch with friends can feel impossible. Enter Beeper, a universal chat app that might just be the ultimate tool for a social media detox.
items.content_html:
In a world where social media algorithms are designed to keep us endlessly scrolling, finding a way to disconnect without losing touch with friends can feel impossible. Enter Beeper, a universal chat app that might just be the ultimate tool for a social media detox.

What is Beeper?

Beeper is a single app that lets you send and receive messages across 14 different chat networks, including WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, iMessage, and Telegram. Available on all major platforms, it syncs your conversations seamlessly so you can manage all your chats in one place.

How Beeper Helps You Detox

While Beeper wasn’t specifically built for social media detoxing, it has become a powerful tool for it. By consolidating your direct messages into one feed, Beeper removes the need to open individual social media apps.

Social media platforms are engineered to capture your attention with endless feeds of videos and images. Beeper bypasses this entirely by only supporting direct messages. You get the convenience of staying in touch with friends across different platforms, without the addictive algorithms and distractions.

Security and Privacy

Beeper is built on the open-source Matrix Protocol, which offers robust end-to-end encryption. While Beeper secures your messages in transit, it is important to remember that your overall security still depends on the individual chat networks you connect to.

Key Privacy Features of the Matrix Protocol:

  • Decentralization: There is no single point of control; anyone can run a Matrix server.
  • End-to-End Encryption: Only the intended recipients can read your messages.
  • Interoperability: Bridges connect Matrix with other platforms, allowing for seamless communication across different services.

By using Beeper, you can maintain your relationships across various networks while successfully distancing yourself from the attention-grabbing mechanics of modern social media.

items.title: A Step-by-Step Guide: Installing RStudio on Vanilla OS 22.10 Kinetic
items.summary: This guide will walk you through the process of installing RStudio on Vanilla OS 22.10 Kinetic using an apt (Ubuntu) container. First, we need to prepare the apt container and install the necessary prerequisites. Open your terminal and run the following commands: Enter the apt…
items.content_html:
This guide will walk you through the process of installing RStudio on Vanilla OS 22.10 Kinetic using an apt (Ubuntu) container.

Initial Setup

First, we need to prepare the apt container and install the necessary prerequisites. Open your terminal and run the following commands:

Enter the apt container:

apx enter apt

Install common software properties:

sudo apt install --no-install-recommends software-properties-common dirmngr

Install required libraries:

sudo apt install libasound2
sudo apt install libnss3

Update and upgrade your system:

sudo apt update
sudo apt upgrade

Downloading and Installing RStudio

Next, download the RStudio Desktop .deb file from the official source: RStudio Desktop 2023.06.2-561

Once the download is complete, install it by running:

cd Downloads
ls
sudo dpkg -i rstudio-2023.06.2-561-amd64.deb

Note: If you encounter any dependency errors during installation, run sudo apt --fix-broken install and then repeat the dpkg command.

Installing R

To run RStudio, you also need to install R. Add the official R repository and install the base package:

Add the R repository:

sudo add-apt-repository "deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs)-cran40/"

Add the public key:

wget -qO- https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/marutter_pubkey.asc | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/cran_ubuntu_key.asc

Install R Base:

sudo apt install r-base

Utilizing RStudio

With everything installed, you can now launch RStudio directly from your terminal by typing:

rstudio

Useful Commands

Command Function
apx enter apt Enters the apt (Ubuntu) container
rstudio Launches the RStudio application
R --version Displays the installed R version
exit Exits the current directory or container
sudo apt update Fetches available updates
sudo apt upgrade Installs available updates

items.title: Bypassing McGraw-Hill’s Copy Protection with NormCap
items.summary: Students have long faced difficulties with McGraw-Hill’s online accounting textbooks due to strict copy prevention measures. This restriction not only prevents offline reading but also hampers studying and taking digital notes on practice problems. While some have attempted to bypass this by changing browser settings,…
items.content_html:
Students have long faced difficulties with McGraw-Hill’s online accounting textbooks due to strict copy prevention measures. This restriction not only prevents offline reading but also hampers studying and taking digital notes on practice problems. While some have attempted to bypass this by changing browser settings, McGraw-Hill uses JavaScript to enforce their copy protection. Fortunately, there is a solution that does not require circumventing their systems: NormCap.

NormCap is an open-source, OCR-powered screenshot tool that allows users to extract text from almost anything on their screen, including images, videos, and protected websites like McGraw-Hill Connect. Instead of capturing a traditional image, NormCap detects and extracts the text directly to your clipboard.

To get started, simply download and install NormCap from their official website. Once running, select the region of text you wish to copy, and it will automatically be added to your clipboard for easy pasting. It is a completely free tool without ads, designed to help students easily capture notes and focus on their coursework.

Step-by-Step Guide

  1. Download and Install Download the application from the official NormCap website.

  2. Launch the Application Start NormCap. A pink border will appear once the necessary permissions are granted.

  3. Select Text Highlight the region of text you wish to copy. The text is now automatically copied to your clipboard.

  4. Paste Your Text Press Ctrl+V (or your system’s paste shortcut) to paste the text anywhere.

Note: Settings can be accessed by starting NormCap or pressing “Capture” in the tray icon while the app is running. As of version 0.4.1, settings are located in the top right corner of the screen.

items.title: How to Convert PDFs to Images with GIMP
items.summary: Introduction Sometimes you may need to convert a PDF to an image PDF, which is a PDF file that contains images instead of text displayed over images. This can be useful for a variety of reasons, such as when you want to preserve the formatting…
items.content_html:
Introduction

Sometimes you may need to convert a PDF to an image PDF, which is a PDF file that contains images instead of text displayed over images. This can be useful for a variety of reasons, such as when you want to preserve the formatting of the original PDF or when you want to share the PDF with others who may not have the same fonts installed on their computer. This can also be used to prevent getting falsely accused of plagiarizing with AI software.

Fortunately, GIMP, the popular open-source image editing software, can be used to easily convert a PDF to an image PDF. Here’s how to do it:

Instructions

  1. Install GIMP First, you need to have GIMP installed on your computer. If you don’t have it already, you can download it for free from the official GIMP website.

  2. Open the PDF File in GIMP Once you have GIMP installed, open it and go to File > Open to open the PDF file you want to convert to an image PDF.

  3. Import Pages as Layers GIMP will show a dialog box asking you how you want to import the PDF file. Choose the Open pages as Layers option, and click Import. GIMP will then import each page of the PDF as a separate image. You can view these images by clicking on the Layers tab on the right-hand side of the screen.

  4. Export as PDF To export the images to an image PDF, go to File > Export As. In the Export Image dialog box, choose a location to save the image PDF file, and give it a name. Under Select File Type, choose PDF from the drop-down menu. Click on the Export button to convert the images to a PDF.

  5. Choose PDF Export Options In the Export Images as PDF dialog box, make sure the Layers as pages (bottom layers first) option is selected, and click Export.

  6. Save the Image PDF File GIMP will then save the image PDF file to the location you specified. You can now view and use the image PDF file just like any other PDF file.

That’s it! With these steps, you can easily convert a PDF to an image PDF using GIMP. Converting a PDF to an image PDF can be a useful skill to have, especially if you work with PDF files frequently. Give it a try and see how it can benefit you!

items.title: The False Positive Problem: A Case Study on GPTZero and AI Detection
items.summary: Introduction In this case study, I explore the high rate of false positives generated by current AI detection software, with a specific focus on GPTZero. After a healthcare professional brought this issue to my attention, I was motivated to look beyond simple bypass methods and…
items.content_html:
Introduction

In this case study, I explore the high rate of false positives generated by current AI detection software, with a specific focus on GPTZero. After a healthcare professional brought this issue to my attention, I was motivated to look beyond simple bypass methods and investigate the practical usability of these tools.

What is GPTZero?

GPTZero identifies AI-generated text by analyzing its complexity and “perplexity”—essentially looking for the unique statistical fingerprints left by large language models.

The False Positives

During my testing, I found that GPTZero yields highly mixed results. While OpenAI’s AI Classifier tends to be more consistent, it offers less detail about which parts of a text are human-written versus AI-generated.

To test GPTZero’s accuracy, I submitted a 2020 medical paper on severe COVID-19 outcomes, authored by multiple CDC contributors. Despite being written well before the widespread use of generative AI, GPTZero flagged more than 50% of the first paragraph as AI-written. Even when testing the maximum allowed 5,000 characters, the false positive rate remained above 50%.

Testing Medical Literature

To further explore this, I tested the abstracts of 20 different neurology papers. The results were shocking: GPTZero flagged 11 out of the 20 human-written abstracts as having AI-generated portions.

The Control: OpenAI’s AI Classifier

Using OpenAI’s AI Classifier as a baseline, I tested the same 2020 COVID-19 paper. The classifier labeled the text as “unclear,” which, while not entirely accurate, is a safer conclusion than a false positive. Given that the paper was published in 2020—and verified as unchanged via the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine—we can be 100% certain it was written without AI assistance.

The Problem with AI Detection

The commercialization of inaccurate AI detection software poses significant risks, particularly in education. If a student is wrongfully accused of plagiarism based on a flawed algorithm, the consequences can be severe. At my university, academic dishonesty is taken very seriously, and false accusations can have a lasting impact on a student’s record. Until these tools become more reliable, their use in high-stakes environments should be heavily scrutinized.

Appendix: Tested Papers Data

items.content_html:
Overview

When your Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05) loses internet access—shown by the globe icon—you can fix the Wi-Fi driver using another computer.

Steps

  1. Prepare another device Use a separate laptop with internet to open Lenovo’s site. Search “Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05) drivers” and download the newest Windows 11 Wi-Fi driver, or use the direct link.

  2. Transfer the driver Insert a USB drive into the working laptop and copy the downloaded file.

  3. Install on the IdeaPad Plug the USB into your Lenovo IdeaPad 5 (14ITL05), open the drive, and double-click 37sw0a0f43gwseb0.exe. Confirm administrator permission if prompted, then complete the installation.

  4. Restart Reboot the laptop so changes take effect.

Notes

  • Check Lenovo’s support site for the latest driver and other updates.
  • Back up essential files before updating.
